apa_citation: Robinson, J. A. (1965). A machine-oriented logic based on the resolution principle. Journal of the ACM, 12(1), 23-41.
method: original method paper introducing the resolution inference rule
key_finding: Introduces resolution as a single complete inference rule for first-order logic refutation proofs
relevance_to_ProofPilot: This is the original paper for the exact resolution-refutation algorithm ProofPilot's search.py and logic.py implement

apa_citation: Corbett, A. T., & Anderson, J. R. (1995). Knowledge tracing: Modeling the acquisition of procedural knowledge. User Modeling and User-Adapted Interaction, 4(4), 253-278.
method: longitudinal study fitting a Bayesian model to student performance data
key_finding: Introduces Bayesian Knowledge Tracing to estimate a student's hidden mastery from a sequence of right/wrong answers
relevance_to_ProofPilot: ProofPilot's bkt.py implements single-skill Bayesian Knowledge Tracing directly from this model

apa_citation: Baker, R. S. J. d., Corbett, A. T., & Aleven, V. (2008). More accurate student modeling through contextual estimation of slip and guess probabilities in Bayesian knowledge tracing. In Proceedings of the 9th International Conference on Intelligent Tutoring Systems (pp. 406-415).
method: machine-learning-based contextual estimation of BKT slip/guess parameters
key_finding: Proposes contextual (per-student, per-context) estimation of slip and guess probabilities instead of one fixed global value
relevance_to_ProofPilot: ProofPilot instead uses the simpler classical fixed global guess/slip (HLD limitation 8) -- this paper is the contrast case for that design decision

apa_citation: Pardos, Z. A., & Heffernan, N. T. (2010). Modeling individualization in a Bayesian networks implementation of knowledge tracing. In User Modeling, Adaptation, and Personalization (UMAP 2010) (pp. 255-266).
method: Bayesian network extension of BKT fit to real tutor log data
key_finding: Individualizing the prior-knowledge parameter per student improves prediction over one fixed BKT prior for all students
relevance_to_ProofPilot: ProofPilot's BKT prior (BKT_P0) is a single assumed constant for all students -- this paper is the contrast case for that simplification

apa_citation: Pavlik, P. I., Cen, H., & Koedinger, K. R. (2009). Performance factors analysis - A new alternative to knowledge tracing. In Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Education (pp. 531-538).
method: logistic regression model of success/failure counts per skill
key_finding: Proposes Performance Factors Analysis, a logistic-regression alternative to BKT that uses counts of prior successes and failures per skill
relevance_to_ProofPilot: An alternative mastery-tracking method ProofPilot did not choose -- useful contrast to justify choosing BKT in the methodology section

apa_citation: Piech, C., Bassen, J., Huang, J., Ganguli, S., Sahami, M., Guibas, L. J., & Sohl-Dickstein, J. (2015). Deep knowledge tracing. In Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 28 (pp. 505-513).
method: recurrent neural network trained on real student interaction logs
key_finding: A recurrent neural network can trace student knowledge without hand-encoded domain structure
limitation: original paper's reported gains were later disputed by follow-up replication work
relevance_to_ProofPilot: ProofPilot deliberately uses classical BKT, not a neural model -- this paper is the counterpoint motivating that choice (simplicity and interpretability over a black-box model)

apa_citation: Khajah, M., Lindsey, R. V., & Mozer, M. C. (2016). How deep is knowledge tracing? In Proceedings of the 9th International Conference on Educational Data Mining (EDM 2016).
theme: comparing deep vs. Bayesian knowledge tracing
method: re-analysis of BKT with added statistical features; benchmarked against deep knowledge tracing
key_finding: Extending classical BKT with recency and inter-skill features matches deep knowledge tracing's predictive performance on the benchmarks tested
limitation: findings are specific to the benchmark datasets used and may not generalize
relevance_to_ProofPilot: Directly supports choosing BKT over a deep-learning model -- a well-specified Bayesian model can match neural performance

apa_citation: Pelanek, R. (2017). Bayesian knowledge tracing, logistic models, and beyond: An overview of learner modeling techniques. User Modeling and User-Adapted Interaction, 27(3-5), 313-350.
method: literature survey comparing many published student-model families
key_finding: not confirmed from abstract (publisher access-gated)
relevance_to_ProofPilot: A survey covering BKT directly -- gives the literature review a map of the wider family of learner models BKT belongs to

apa_citation: VanLehn, K. (2006). The behavior of tutoring systems. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education, 16(3), 227-265.
method: conceptual analysis of tutoring system behaviour across multiple published systems
key_finding: Tutoring systems commonly operate as two nested loops: an outer loop selecting the next task and an inner loop giving step-level feedback and hints
limitation: descriptive framework, not an empirical evaluation of one specific system
relevance_to_ProofPilot: ProofPilot's hint ladder (step-level feedback within one exercise) and next-exercise selection (BKT-driven) map directly onto VanLehn's inner-loop/outer-loop framework

apa_citation: VanLehn, K. (2011). The relative effectiveness of human tutoring, intelligent tutoring systems, and other tutoring systems. Educational Psychologist, 46(4), 197-221.
method: meta-analysis of published effect sizes for tutoring system types
key_finding: Reports an effect size of d=0.79 for human tutoring and d=0.76 for intelligent tutoring systems
relevance_to_ProofPilot: Motivates building a step-level automated tutor as a near-human-effective alternative to one-to-one tutoring

apa_citation: Kulik, J. A., & Fletcher, J. D. (2016). Effectiveness of intelligent tutoring systems: A meta-analytic review. Review of Educational Research, 86(1), 42-78.
method: meta-analysis of 50 controlled evaluations of intelligent tutoring systems
key_finding: Median effect of intelligent tutoring was to raise test scores 0.66 standard deviations over conventional instruction
limitation: improvement depended heavily on whether the outcome test was locally developed or standardized
relevance_to_ProofPilot: Supports the premise that a working ITS (even a narrow-domain one like ProofPilot) can produce a measurable learning benefit

apa_citation: Ma, W., Adesope, O. O., Nesbit, J. C., & Liu, Q. (2014). Intelligent tutoring systems and learning outcomes: A meta-analysis. Journal of Educational Psychology, 106(4), 901-918.
method: meta-analysis of 107 effect sizes from 14321 participants across multiple ITS studies
key_finding: Effect sizes varied by ITS type, comparison condition, outcome type, and whether the knowledge was procedural or declarative
relevance_to_ProofPilot: ProofPilot targets a specifically procedural skill (resolution proof construction) -- this paper's procedural/declarative split is directly relevant to interpreting any future pilot results

apa_citation: Black, P., & Wiliam, D. (1998). Assessment and classroom learning. Assessment in Education: Principles, Policy & Practice, 5(1), 7-74.
method: literature review of classroom formative-assessment studies
key_finding: Innovations that strengthen the frequency and quality of feedback students receive about their learning produce substantial learning gains
relevance_to_ProofPilot: Motivates ProofPilot's step-level named feedback (vs. a single right/wrong grade) as a formative-assessment design

apa_citation: Hattie, J., & Timperley, H. (2007). The power of feedback. Review of Educational Research, 77(1), 81-112.
method: narrative synthesis proposing a model of feedback levels
key_finding: Feedback is most effective when it addresses goal, progress, and next steps at the task, process, self-regulation, or self level
relevance_to_ProofPilot: ProofPilot's named step-level diagnosis (e.g. NO_CLASH) is task/process-level feedback this model classifies and justifies

apa_citation: Shute, V. J. (2008). Focus on formative feedback. Review of Educational Research, 78(1), 153-189.
method: literature review synthesizing formative-feedback research
key_finding: Effective formative feedback should be nonevaluative, supportive, timely, and specific
relevance_to_ProofPilot: ProofPilot's messages.yaml feedback names each mistake without a grade, matching these four properties

apa_citation: Bloom, B. S. (1984). The 2 sigma problem: The search for methods of group instruction as effective as one-to-one tutoring. Educational Researcher, 13(6), 4-16.
method: comparative experimental study of mastery learning plus tutoring vs. conventional instruction
key_finding: One-to-one tutored students performed about two standard deviations above conventionally taught students
relevance_to_ProofPilot: Classic motivation for building an automated step-level tutor as a scalable approximation of one-to-one tutoring

apa_citation: Brown, J. S., & Burton, R. R. (1978). Diagnostic models for procedural bugs in basic mathematical skills. Cognitive Science, 2(2), 155-192.
method: diagnostic system (BUGGY) built from a library of procedural mal-rules
key_finding: Student arithmetic errors can be explained as systematic application of specific incorrect sub-procedures rather than random mistakes
relevance_to_ProofPilot: Directly analogous to ProofPilot's named resolution-mistake codes, which diagnose a specific logical misstep rather than just marking an answer wrong

apa_citation: Barnes, T., & Stamper, J. (2008). Toward automatic hint generation for logic proof tutoring using historical student data. In Proceedings of the 9th International Conference on Intelligent Tutoring Systems (pp. 373-382).
theme: automatic hint generation for logic proof tutoring
method: Markov decision process built from historical student proof-attempt data
key_finding: Proposes using a Markov decision process over historical student data to automatically generate hints in a logic proof tutor
relevance_to_ProofPilot: Direct precedent: this is a logic-proof-tutor hint-generation paper in the same problem space as ProofPilot's resolution hint ladder, though ProofPilot's hints are rule/search-derived rather than data-mined

apa_citation: Stamper, J., Eagle, M., Barnes, T., & Croy, M. (2013). Experimental evaluation of automatic hint generation for a logic tutor. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education, 22(1-2), 3-17.
theme: automatic hint generation for logic proof tutoring
method: controlled experiment (switching-replications design) evaluating data-driven hints in a logic tutor
key_finding: Automatically generated data-driven hints helped students persist through a deductive logic proof tutor
relevance_to_ProofPilot: Direct empirical precedent for evaluating whether ProofPilot's hint ladder helps students complete resolution proofs

apa_citation: Bull, S., & Kay, J. (2007). Student models that invite the learner in: The SMILI open learner modelling framework. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education, 17(2), 89-120.
method: framework paper proposing a structure for describing and comparing open learner models
key_finding: Proposes the SMILI framework for systematically describing, comparing, and critiquing open learner models (student-visible models of their own knowledge)
relevance_to_ProofPilot: ProofPilot's MasteryBars component (visible per-skill mastery percentages) is an open learner model -- this is the framework paper for that design category

apa_citation: Aleven, V., McLaren, B., Roll, I., & Koedinger, K. (2006). Toward meta-cognitive tutoring: A model of help seeking with a cognitive tutor. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education, 16(2), 101-128.
method: cognitive-tutor-based model of when and how students should seek help
key_finding: Proposes a computational model for judging appropriate help-seeking behaviour (e.g. unproductive guessing vs. productive hint requests)
relevance_to_ProofPilot: AMBIGUOUS MATCH for the seed citation Aleven et al. 2006 -- see L21b for the second candidate found. Relevant to ProofPilot's hint-request/mastery-penalty design (a hint lowers the scored mastery gain).

apa_citation: Aleven, V., McLaren, B. M., Sewall, J., & Koedinger, K. R. (2006). The Cognitive Tutor Authoring Tools (CTAT): Preliminary evaluation of efficiency gains. In Proceedings of the 8th International Conference on Intelligent Tutoring Systems (pp. 61-70).
method: preliminary efficiency evaluation of an authoring toolkit for cognitive tutors
key_finding: Reports preliminary efficiency gains from using the CTAT authoring toolkit to build cognitive tutors
relevance_to_ProofPilot: SECOND AMBIGUOUS MATCH for Aleven et al. 2006 -- both L21a and L21b are real, verified, first-authored-by-Aleven 2006 papers. The student must pick which one was actually intended/read; do not cite both as if they were the same paper.

apa_citation: Baker, R. S., Corbett, A. T., & Koedinger, K. R. (2004). Detecting student misuse of intelligent tutoring systems. In Proceedings of the 7th International Conference on Intelligent Tutoring Systems (pp. 531-540).
method: log-based detection method for students misusing a tutor (e.g. systematic guessing)
key_finding: Proposes methods to automatically detect when students are gaming an intelligent tutoring system rather than engaging with it
relevance_to_ProofPilot: Relevant to ProofPilot's never-guess design principle and its hint-cost mastery penalty, which are both aimed at discouraging unproductive interaction patterns

apa_citation: Doignon, J.-P., & Falmagne, J.-C. (1999). Knowledge spaces. Springer.
method: mathematical/theoretical monograph defining knowledge structures and spaces
key_finding: Formalizes a mathematical theory of knowledge states and the feasible orderings in which skills can be acquired
relevance_to_ProofPilot: Relevant background theory for any discussion of how ProofPilot's exercise-selection/mastery-threshold design relates to formal models of knowledge structure

apa_citation: Russell, S. J., & Norvig, P. (2020). Artificial intelligence: A modern approach (4th ed.). Pearson.
method: textbook
key_finding: not verified beyond edition/publisher/year confirmed via Pearson's own catalog page
limitation: textbook breadth; not a single empirical claim
relevance_to_ProofPilot: Standard course reference for the propositional logic, resolution, and breadth-first search material ProofPilot's core directly implements (syllabus Units 2 and 4)
